correctness.rationale: In stationary renewal occupation, a cycle of dimensionless length S contributes one unit of age density at each v<S; division by E S=1 gives f_V(v)=Pr(S>v), including for a deterministic clock with equilibrium random phase. The selected square wave has first-harmonic amplitude 4B/pi; at observation the phase is shifted by the age, and visibility restricts v to at least d=r tau. Thus H is the magnitude of the truncated age transform at z=omega/r. Integration of the tail gives E V=E S^2/2 and E V^2=E S^3/3. The omitted integral equals d+o(d), with imaginary or phase error bounded by |z|d^2/2; expanding the full transform and its modulus gives the joint loss d+Var(V) z^2/2+o(d+z^2). For each fixed positive omega the transform is continuous in r, vanishes at infinity by the age tail and at zero by Riemann–Lebesgue plus the vanishing omitted mass. A rate proportional to omega^(2/3) achieves loss O(omega^(2/3)). Any optimizer then has omitted mass O(omega^(2/3)), hence r=O(omega^(2/3)) since f_V tends to one at zero. The full transform has magnitude within O(omega^(2/3)) of one by the triangle inequality. Its absolute continuity, strict modulus below one away from zero and decay at infinity force z to zero, then its positive quadratic modulus deficit gives z^2=O(omega^(2/3)). This puts every optimizer on a common compact interval after rescaling r by omega^(2/3). The uniform joint expansion there reduces the limit to the unique minimum of tau y+Var(V)/(2 y^2), with the stated optimizer and loss coefficients. Cauchy–Schwarz gives E S^3 >= (E S^2)^2 and E S^2 >= 1 with equality of the latter only for S=1; thus Var(V) >= 1/12 with precisely that equality case. The exponential and Erlang moments give the stated benchmarks. Read the numerical checker without executing it; its finite grid/local optimization is not a certificate for the all-global-optimizers assertion.
